Challenge: Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map
About Us: We are a complete, multidisciplinary team tackling the Martian Map challenge for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Bringing together skills in full-stack development, geospatial data visualization, UI/UX design, and planetary science research, we are excited to combine open NASA datasets to build practical tools that support human exploration in The Next Frontier.
summary: Our project, Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map (AresPath HUD), is designed to help astronauts explore Mars safely and efficiently. We developed an interactive Martian map that shows important locations, three main waypoints, routes, distance, slopes and estimated walking time. It also includes an Astronaut Health and Safety system that displays important information such as oxygen levels, spacesuit battery, radiation and temperature. The map highlights rocky areas, possible dangers and safe locations. Our project uses NASA-inspired information and simulated readings to support mission planning. This project is important because Mars has a challenging environment, and astronauts need proper guidance and safety information. Our goal is to make future Mars exploration safer, smarter and easier.
details:
Our project, Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map (AresPath HUD), is an interactive system designed to help astronauts explore Mars safely.

It provides a Martian navigation map with three waypoints, showing routes, distance, slope, walking time, suit energy and oxygen usage. It also includes an astronaut health and safety dashboard that displays oxygen levels, spacesuit battery, radiation dose and local temperature.

The system uses four simulated data layers inspired by NASA instruments:

  • HiRISE: Provides detailed Martian terrain imagery.
  • Topographic DTM: Shows slopes and possible walking hazards.
  • CRISM: Displays mineral information.
  • RAD and MEDA: Provide radiation and dust information.

The website also includes a helmet visor view, rover tablet view and simulated dust storm and solar storm alerts.

Our project aims to make Mars exploration safer and help astronauts make better decisions using scientific information and technology.
